issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s protected status acquired under an earlier tenancy law does not survive under the replacement tenancy law for land leased from a local authority when the replacement law expressly excludes such leases from its protections.
material_facts: The tenant leased agricultural land from a municipality and became a protected tenant under the earlier tenancy law because the municipality did not seek a declaration that he was not protected.
The replacement tenancy law excluded land held on lease from a local authority from its preceding provisions, including the provision that recognised tenants protected under the earlier law.
The tenant relied on the replacement law’s saving provision for rights acquired before its commencement.
The later provision that replaced the recognition provision after amendment also did not apply to land leased from a local authority.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not claim protected-tenant status under the replacement law; the saving provision did not preserve his earlier status against the express exclusion for leases from local authorities, and the amended recognition provision did not assist him.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 31, 88(1)(a) and 89(2)(b) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, section 31’s recognition of persons protected under sections 3, 3-A or 4 of the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939, did not apply to land held on lease from a local authority. The saving provision preserved earlier rights only save as expressly provided in the 1948 Act; section 88(1)(a) was such an express provision. Sections 3, 3-A and 4 of the 1939 Act continued in modified form in Schedule I for the purpose of section 31, but did not create new protected tenants under the 1948 Act. Section 4-A, which replaced section 31 after the 1956 amendment, likewise did not apply to such leases. Sakharam v. Manikchand was disapproved; Mohanlal Chunilal Kothari v. Tribhovan Haribhai Tamboli was explained, and its distinction between clauses (a)–(c) and clause (d) of section 88(1) was rejected.

rule.if: protected_tenancy_status_claim and earlier_protected_status and local_authority_lease and ordinary_tenancy_protections_expressly_excluded

predicates.protected_tenancy_status_claim: A tenant sought recognition of protected-tenant status under the governing tenancy framework.
predicates.earlier_protected_status: The tenant had acquired protected-tenant status under an earlier tenancy framework before the replacement framework began.
predicates.local_authority_lease: The land for which protection was claimed was held by the tenant on lease from a local public authority.
predicates.ordinary_tenancy_protections_expressly_e: The replacement framework expressly excluded the ordinary tenancy protections from applying to land leased from a local public authority.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks recognition of earlier protected status for land leased from a local public authority, and the replacement framework expressly excludes its ordinary protections from such land, the earlier status is not recognized under that framework.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory protection introduced after a tenancy has already been determined does not protect the former tenant in proceedings concerning that tenancy.
material_facts: The landlord gave notice terminating the tenancy effective March 31, 1956.
The provision relied on for protection came into force on April 1, 1956, after the tenancy had been determined.
The tenant sought a declaration of protected-tenant status while proceedings concerning possession of the land were pending.
issues.conclusion: The later-introduced provision did not protect the tenant because the lease had already been determined before that provision came into force.
issues.legal_principle: Section 88-B of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, introduced by the 1956 amendment, did not protect the tenant because his lease had already been determined before section 88-B came into force on April 1, 1956.

predicates.pending_tenancy_protection_claim: A tenant sought statutory protection while proceedings concerning the tenancy or possession of the land were pending.
predicates.lease_determined_before_new_protection_b: The landlord had determined the lease before the new statutory protection came into force.

issues.definition: If a tenant seeks protection in pending proceedings after the lease was determined before the new protection began, the new protection does not protect the former tenant.
